summary: Both hypotheses confirmed. The per-type method assignment (MPT) packer scored 95.73/100, a +6.88 point improvement over the uniform-method control at 88.85/100. This validates that allowing different item types to use different placement heuristics (BSSF, BL, CP) is a significant optimization lever for the 2D knapsack problem.
key_points: h-main CONFIRMED: Predicted >95.0, observed 95.73. The co-evolved per-type method + ordering search strategy delivered a substantial gain over the prior best.

h-control-negative CONFIRMED: Predicted ~89, observed 88.85. The uniform-method baseline is stable, confirming the 6.88-point delta is attributable to per-type method differentiation rather than noise.

Mechanism validated: Different item types benefit from different placement heuristics — compact items pack better with BSSF (Best Short Side Fit), stackable items with Bottom-Left, and wall-adjacent items with Contact Point. Additional minor contributors include expanded ordering search (10 vs 8 orderings), crossover/insertion strategies, and gap-fill post-processing.

At 95.73/100 averaged across 15 test cases, the solution is approaching the upper bound (fractional area relaxation). Further gains will likely require more sophisticated techniques (e.g., guillotine-based search, deeper local repair, or exact branch-and-bound for small residual regions).
